messages:
maria: Heads-up — ACME reported intermittent 502s from the API during today's canary rollout (us-east-1). They gave a request id in the response header: req_01GZ9Y8K5A2. Anyone on call?

devon: On it. Can you paste the full request-id + the exact curl they used so I can start repro?

maria: Full request id above. Their curl they sent:
```
curl -sS -X POST \"https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood/gptx-3.2q-canary\",\"input\":\"Summarize the attached doc in two bullets.\"}'
```

josh: FYI: rollout config shows gptx-3.2q-canary at ~15% in us-east-1. Fallback is to redwood/gptx-3.1-stable. Pulling logs for req_01GZ9Y8K5A2 now.

sre-bot: debug-bundle created: https://internal.debug/dbg-779 (contains runtime logs, kernel traces, request spans for req_01GZ9Y8K5A2) :package:

maria: Customer also pasted the error body they saw:
```
{
  \"error\": \"upstream read timeout\",
  \"code\": 502,
  \"request_id\": \"req_01GZ9Y8K5A2\"
}
```

sarah: I pulled dbg-779. Quick grep around req_01GZ9Y8K5A2 shows repeated lines: 
```
[2026-03-17T15:02:14Z] WARN kernel: kv cache mismatch detected for shard=3, req=req_01GZ9Y8K5A2
[2026-03-17T15:02:14Z] ERROR runtime: upstream read timeout after 10s
```
Looks correlated with the error spikes.

devon: Can we repro locally/staging with the same canary variant and the customer's prompt? @josh can you run a controlled test: canary, stable, and pinned model?

josh: Running curl against the canary pool now with the exact payload. Will collect headers + response. ETA ~15m.

tier2-oncall: If you provide the prompt + headers I'll run across three variants and enable verbose curl (-i) to capture x-request-id + upstream headers. Also can toggle model-level cache flag on the canary group.

maria: Prompt the customer sent: \"Summarize Q1 roadmap and call out any blockers for delivery.\"

josh: Repro steps I used:
```
curl -i -X POST \"https://canary.api.redwood.dev/v1/generate\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-TEST\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood/gptx-3.2q-canary\",\"input\":\"Summarize Q1 roadmap and call out any blockers for delivery.\"}'
```
Results: 502 returned twice with headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
X-Request-ID: req_01GZ9Y8K5A2
Upstream-Status: 502
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"upstream read timeout","request_id":"req_01GZ9Y8K5A2"}
```

devon: Hypothesis: kernel selection / KV cache warmup race on the canary path leading to timeouts under load. If true, disabling the prefix/KV cache for the canary variant should avoid the race. @tier2-oncall can you toggle cache=false on the canary model group and re-run josh's test?

tier2-oncall: Toggled cache=false for redwood/gptx-3.2q-canary in us-east-1. Re-running the 20-request test now.

sarah: Note — stable (redwood/gptx-3.1-stable) shows zero 502s for the same prompt in our logs. That matches customer claim that pinning to stable helped earlier.

josh: Update: after disabling the cache, canary requests succeeded 20/20. No 502s, responses returned in ~600-900ms. Looks like the KV cache warmup path is implicated. I'll collect a fresh debug bundle and attach.

devon: Good repro. Next steps: create a fix + lock for cache warmup or serializing kernel selection for hot shards. Also create incident ticket and recommend customer pin to stable until patch lands.

maria: Customer is OK with pinning. I sent them this curl snippet to pin: 
```
curl -sS -X POST \"https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood/gptx-3.1-stable\",\"input\":\"Summarize Q1 roadmap...\"}'
```

josh: I opened PR #2847 to add a lock+metrics around KV cache warmups and created incident I-2026-142. Added the dbg-779 + new bundle dbg-791 as attachments.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll close the support ticket once the customer confirms stable pin works for 24h and we'll keep the canary disabled for that model until the fix lands. Leaving logs in dbg-779 and dbg-791. :thumbsup:
